precepts.text: Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer: here is the worldly sorrow. When the affliction increases, after being wicked the whole time, now you are calling on the Lord, and the line is no longer available. For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord: they would none of my counsel; they despised all my reproof. Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way: if you are out there sowing sin, that is what you are going to reap.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Paul says “the sorrow of the world worketh death.” Here is what that worldly sorrow looks like: “Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me”. When the Lord increases the affliction, after you have been wicked the whole time, now you are calling on the Lord: it's getting real down here, the persecution is on, I ain't got no food. You call, and the line says the number you have dialed is no longer available to you, dummy. You'll seek him early, like getting on a pre-call, and you still won't find him. You won't have any connection to the Lord on that day.

Why? “For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord”. They had the carnal mind, the mind of Cain and Esau, and cast the word behind their back like their father did. “They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof.” They literally threw the word behind their back, and a lot of our brothers and sisters do that. We all have to examine ourselves.

“Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.” If you are out there sowing sin, that is what you are going to reap.

That is Esau's sorrow. He sold his birthright, then realized, damn, I want that blessing back, and cried bitterly over what he himself threw away. So we have to be sincere when we come to the Lord and have the real godly sorrow that works repentance to salvation, to our inheritance, not to be repented of. We can't be out here faking the funk.

precepts.text: Having these promises, cleanse yourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God. We have wronged no man, corrupted no man, defrauded no man. We do this in the fear of God's judgment.
precepts.point: Come out from among them and be ye separate, touch not the unclean thing, and I will receive you and be a father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
Chapter 6 ends with promises: “I will receive you, And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.” Then Paul says what those promises require: “Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.”

That is why we come out from among them, are separate and touch not the unclean thing. We are not unequally yoked with unbelievers, because righteousness has no fellowship with unrighteousness and light has no communion with darkness. If your best friend is somebody in the world who just finished celebrating Christmas, you are not in the truth, and that goes for you sisters too. You are lying to yourself, just putting on the purple and the fringes.

“Receive us; we have wronged no man, we have corrupted no man, we have defrauded no man.” That is the minister who gives no offence in any thing, so that the ministry is not blamed. Do not be the leader who is out there selling drugs, a murderer, a thief, the setback to this.

We cleanse ourselves in the fear of God's judgment. Much is given and much is required. God sent his Son to bear our sins, made us his friends and his ambassadors, and gave us the laws of God. If we then live in hypocrisy, it is not a few stripes for us. Now is the accepted time and now is the day of salvation: are we going to waste it?

precepts.text: Godly sorrow worketh repentance unto salvation, but the sorrow of the world worketh death.
precepts.point: Through David's judgment, Solomon was still able to be born; it was all part of the plan of the Most High. The backup master plan behind everything was Christ, who still had to be born through David's lineage; David was still loved and still forgiven, which shows repentance, and that even the mighty among us can fall and yet rise back up.

note.label: 2 Samuel 12: Nathan's Parable and the Judgment on David's House

precepts.why:
“For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.”

David’s sorrow was godly sorrow, and it worked repentance. Through the judgment, “David comforted Bath–sheba his wife”, and she bare a son, “and he called his name Solomon: and the Lord loved him.” The Lord sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, who called his name Jedidiah, “because of the Lord.”

David was still loved and still forgiven, and that shows repentance. Through David’s judgment Solomon was still able to be born; it was all part of the plan of the Most High. The backup master plan behind everything was Christ, who still had to be born through David’s lineage.

precepts.text: Answering whether we must be angry with ourselves for breaking God's laws: godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of, but the sorrow of the world worketh death, so be angry enough to repent and change, not to beat yourself down.
precepts.point: Repentance is for Israel; when he blots out the sins he is speaking of Jacob, the servants that sinned whom God is calling back. Sing O ye heavens, shout ye lower parts of the earth, break forth into singing, for the Lord hath redeemed Jacob and glorified himself in Israel.

note.label: Isaiah 44: The Idol Maker's Folly and the Changed Name

precepts.why:
“I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions, and, as a cloud, thy sins: return unto me; for I have redeemed thee.” Repentance is for Israel; when he blots out the sins he is speaking of Jacob, the servants that sinned whom God is calling back. So must we be angry with ourselves for breaking God’s laws? Paul answers: “Now I rejoice, not that ye were made sorry, but that ye sorrowed to repentance: for ye were made sorry after a godly manner, that ye might receive damage by us in nothing. For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.”

Godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of, but the sorrow of the world worketh death. So be angry enough to repent and change, not to beat yourself down. The sorrow that returns you to him is the godly sorrow; then the heavens sing and the lower parts of the earth shout, “for the Lord hath redeemed Jacob, and glorified himself in Israel.”
